units: starts, completions, blocks, downs and lead times in model minutes; Result members in ticks (1 ms)
notes: downs are [resource, unit (failure clock), from, to] in the order the downtimes started, to null when still down at the horizon (or at the stall); pending are [resource, unit, minute] of the failures that found no idle unit and waited for a released or repaired unit (finish-first, D-051; D-074 (a) B); service_start_seqs, where given, are [entity, minute, sequence number of the dispatch event that started the service] and events the number of events the replication processed (T-048 review round 2, L2). Each case's derivation is the hand derivation of its expected values (assembled by checks/evidence/2026-10-25-T-048/breakdown_goldens_gen.py, which only builds the JSON).

cases.title: two units: a repaired unit goes to a waiting failure (12), two waiting failures take the two next released units in the order they fired while a held request stays held (25, 26), the next repair with no failure waiting wakes it (27) (D-074 (a) B; review round 1, M1). ADR-026's planned G-F3 scenario is G-F3b
derivation: Re-derived in T-048 review round 1 under D-074 (a) option B: a unit that becomes available, released by a job or repaired, goes to the waiting failures first, in the order they fired; only a unit no failure waits for wakes the held front.

Under option A this case held ADR-026 D-051's planned G-F3 ('2 unit、一個等待中的故障、兩次釋放：第一個被釋放的 unit 停機、第二個變成可用') at 22-26. Under B the repair at 12 gives failure 1 its unit, clock 1 next fails at 24, and at 26 the second release goes to that second waiting failure, so the scenario is no longer here; it is G-F3b (T-048 review round 2, L1). This case now covers a repair serving a waiting failure, two waiting failures served FIFO by two releases while a held request is decided again and stays held, and a repair with no failure waiting that wakes the held request.
m has capacity 2: two failure clocks, units 0 and 1, both TTF 10 and TTR 2. Five one-off sources: s1 at 8, s2 at 18, s3 at 19, s4 at 23, s5 at 28; service 7.
t=0: the five first arrivals (source ID order), then FAILURE(0) at 10 and FAILURE(1) at 10 (unit order, so 0's has the smaller sequence).
t=8: s1/1 [8,15]. t=10: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1: unit down (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 12; FAILURE(1): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits.
t=12: REPAIR(0): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 22; the repaired unit goes to the waiting failure 1: down (D=1), REPAIR(1) at 14. (Under option A it would wait for s1/1's release at 15.)
t=14: REPAIR(1): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 24; no failure waits, no request is held. t=15: s1/1 completes; nothing waits.
t=18: s2/1 [18,25]. t=19: s3/1 [19,26] (both units in use). t=22: FAILURE(0): idle 0, waits. t=23: s4/1 held (in use 2). t=24: FAILURE(1): idle 0, waits behind failure 0.
t=25: s2/1 completes (0): its unit goes down for the first waiting failure, 0 (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 27; s4/1 wakes, but in use 1 (s3/1) + 1 > C - D = 2 - 1: held.
t=26: s3/1 completes: its unit goes down for failure 1 (D=2), REPAIR(1) at 28; s4/1 wakes, in use 0 + 1 > 2 - 2: held.
t=27: REPAIR(0): D=1, FAILURE(0) at 37; no failure waits, so the unit wakes s4/1: 0 + 1 <= 2 - 1: s4/1 [27,34].
t=28: ARRIVAL s5/1 (10) queues and is a candidate; REPAIR(1) (15): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 38, wakes nothing (s5/1 is not held); DISPATCH (20): s5/1 [28,35].

t=34: s4/1 completes; t=35: s5/1 completes; nothing waits. t=37: FAILURE(0): idle 2, down, REPAIR(0) at 39. t=38: FAILURE(1): idle 1, down, REPAIR(1) at 40. t=39: REPAIR(0), FAILURE(0) at 49 (> horizon). t=40: REPAIR(1) (at the horizon), FAILURE(1) at 50 (> horizon).

Result over [0, 40]: 5 completed, lead times 7,7,7,11,7, waits 0,0,0,4,0; in use 5 x 7 = 35 min, utilization 35/80; down [10,12], [12,14], [25,27], [26,28], [37,39], [38,40]: 12 min (both units down on [26,27]), 6 started, 6 complete repairs of 12 min; available = 2*40 - 12 = 68 min; idle = 68 - 35 = 33 min.

cases.title: ADR-026 D-051's planned G-F3 under D-074 (a) B: two units, one waiting failure, two releases with no repair between them; the first released unit goes down, the second becomes available (T-048 review round 2, L1)
derivation: ADR-026 D-051's planned G-F3 ('2 unit、一個等待中的故障、兩次釋放：第一個被釋放的 unit 停機、第二個變成可用'), which G-F3 lost under option B (see G-F3). It is at 25-27: one failure waits while both units are in use and none is down; then two job releases with no repair between them; the first released unit goes down for the failure, the second becomes available and the held s4/1 starts on it.

m has capacity 2, both clocks TTF 10 and TTR 5; four one-off sources s1 at 8, s2 at 21, s3 at 22, s4 at 24; service 5. Ticks 8-18 only put clock 1 three minutes behind clock 0 (a failure that waits for a release, as in G-F2), so that at 25 one clock fails while the other is up. Sequence numbers in parentheses.
t=0: arrivals s1 at 8 (1), s2 at 21 (2), s3 at 22 (3), s4 at 24 (4) in source ID order; then FAILURE(0) at 10 (5), FAILURE(1) at 10 (6).
t=8: s1/1 queues, DISPATCH (7): s1/1 [8,13] (completion 8). t=10: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1: down (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 15 (9); FAILURE(1): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits.

t=13: s1/1 completes: the released unit goes down for the waiting failure 1 (D=2), REPAIR(1) at 18 (10); DISPATCH (11) grants nothing. t=15: REPAIR(0): D=1, FAILURE(0) at 25 (12); no failure waits, nothing is held. t=18: REPAIR(1): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 28 (13).
t=21: s2/1 queues, DISPATCH (14): s2/1 [21,26] (completion 15). t=22: s3/1, DISPATCH (16): s3/1 [22,27] (completion 17). t=24: s4/1 queues, DISPATCH (18): in use 2 + 1 > C - D = 2: held.
t=25: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 2 = 0: waits. It is the only waiting failure: nothing is down and clock 1 is up until 28.
t=26: s2/1 completes, the first release: its unit goes down for failure 0 (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 31 (19); s4/1 wakes and DISPATCH (20) decides it again: in use 1 + 1 > 2 - 1: held.

t=27: s3/1 completes, the second release: no failure waits, so the unit becomes available; s4/1 wakes, DISPATCH (21): 0 + 1 <= 2 - 1: s4/1 [27,32] (completion 22). No repair came between the two releases (REPAIR(0) is at 31, clock 1 fails at 28).

t=28: FAILURE(1): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits. t=31: REPAIR(0): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 41 (> horizon, no sequence); the repaired unit goes to failure 1 (option B): D=1, REPAIR(1) at 36 (23). t=32: s4/1 completes, DISPATCH (24) grants nothing. t=36: REPAIR(1): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 46 (> horizon). 24 events.

Result over [0, 40] (T = 40, C = 2): 4 completed, lead times 5,5,5,8 (s4/1 from 24 to 32), waits 0,0,0,3; in use 4 x 5 = 20 min, utilization 20/80; down [10,15], [13,18], [26,31], [31,36]: 20 min (both units down on [13,15]), 4 started, 4 complete repairs of 20 min; available = 80 - 20 = 60 min; idle = 60 - 20 = 40 min (16 on [0,8], 2 on [8,10], 3 on [15,18], 6 on [18,21], 1 on [21,22], 4 on [32,36], 8 on [36,40]).

cases.title: a repair satisfies a waiting failure (D-074 (a) B; the reviewer's N8, T-048 review round 1, M1)
derivation: m has capacity 2, both clocks TTF 10 and TTR 5; one entity arrives at 1 and is served for 100 min, so it holds one unit to the horizon (its completion at 101 is not scheduled). Option B: a repaired unit goes to the waiting failures first.
t=0: s1's arrival at 1, then FAILURE(0) and FAILURE(1) at 10. t=1: s1/1 queues, the dispatch grants it: in use 1.
t=10: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1: down (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 15; FAILURE(1): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits.
t=15: REPAIR(0): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 25; the repaired unit goes to the waiting failure 1: down (D=1), REPAIR(1) at 20.
t=20: REPAIR(1): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 30. t=25: FAILURE(0): idle 1: down, REPAIR(0) at 30.
t=30: FAILURE(1) (scheduled at 20) runs before REPAIR(0) (scheduled at 25): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0, waits; REPAIR(0): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 40, the unit goes to failure 1: down, REPAIR(1) at 35.

The pattern repeats every 15 min: t=35 REPAIR(1), FAILURE(1) at 45; t=40 FAILURE(0) down, REPAIR(0) at 45; t=45 FAILURE(1) waits, REPAIR(0) gives it the unit (REPAIR(1) at 50), FAILURE(0) at 55; t=50 REPAIR(1), FAILURE(1) at 60; t=55 FAILURE(0) down, REPAIR(0) at 60; t=60 FAILURE(1) waits, REPAIR(0) (FAILURE(0) at 70, not scheduled) gives it the unit, whose REPAIR(1) at 65 is after the horizon.

Downs: [0,10,15], [1,15,20], [0,25,30], [1,30,35], [0,40,45], [1,45,50], [0,55,60], [1,60,-]; waiting failures: clock 1 at 10, 30, 45, 60 (the last three wait 0 minutes: the repair comes later in the same tick).

Result over [0, 60] (T = 60, C = 2): in use 59 min (s1/1 from 1); D = 1 on [10,20], [25,35], [40,50], [55,60]: down 35 min; 8 downtimes started (the one at 60 too); 7 complete repairs of 35 min (the one from 60 is not repaired by H); available = 120 - 35 = 85 min; idle = 85 - 59 = 26 min; utilization 59/120. Nothing completes: no lead time; s1/1's queue wait 0.
Under option A (the repaired unit does not go to the waiting failure, review N8): failure 1 waits from 10 to the horizon while clock 0 fails at 10, 25, 40, 55: down 20 min, 4 started, idle 41 min.

cases.title: G-F9 with TTR 10 = TTF: a repair schedules its own next failure before the repair of the failure it serves, so in each later tick that failure comes first and waits (SIMULATION_SPEC §3 REPAIR; T-048 review round 2, L2)
derivation: The reviewer's n8eq (T-048 review round 2, L2): G-F9's model with TTR 10. With TTR = TTF the FAILURE that a repair schedules and the REPAIR of the waiting failure it serves fall in the same tick, so their sequence numbers (the order SIMULATION_SPEC §3 gives REPAIR: draw the next TTF and schedule FAILURE(u) first, then serve the waiting failures) decide which runs first. Sequence numbers in parentheses.
t=0: s1's arrival at 1 (1), FAILURE(0) at 10 (2), FAILURE(1) at 10 (3). t=1: s1/1 queues, DISPATCH (4) grants it: one unit in use to the horizon (its completion at 101 is not scheduled).
t=10: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1: down (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 20 (5); FAILURE(1): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits.
t=20: REPAIR(0): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 30 (6); then the unit goes to the waiting failure 1: D=1, REPAIR(1) at 30 (7).
t=30: FAILURE(0) (6) runs before REPAIR(1) (7): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits; REPAIR(1): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 40 (8), the unit goes to failure 0: D=1, REPAIR(0) at 40 (9).

The same every 10 min with the clocks swapped: t=40 FAILURE(1) (8) waits, REPAIR(0) (9): FAILURE(0) at 50 (10), REPAIR(1) at 50 (11); t=50 FAILURE(0) (10) waits, REPAIR(1) (11): FAILURE(1) at 60 (12), REPAIR(0) at 60 (13); t=60 FAILURE(1) (12) waits, REPAIR(0) (13): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 70 (> horizon, not scheduled), the unit goes to failure 1: D=1, REPAIR(1) at 70 (not scheduled). 13 events.
Waiting failures: clock 1 at 10, 0 at 30, 1 at 40, 0 at 50, 1 at 60 (the last four wait 0 minutes). Downs: [0,10,20], [1,20,30], [0,30,40], [1,40,50], [0,50,60], [1,60,-].

Had the repair served the waiting failure before scheduling its own next failure, at 20 REPAIR(1) at 30 would take 6 and FAILURE(0) at 30 7; at 30 the repair would run first and find no failure waiting, and FAILURE(0) would then find the unit idle: the waiting failures would be 1 at 10, 1 at 40 and 1 at 60 only. The downs and the Result would be the same; this list (compared entry by entry) and the sequence numbers tell the two orders apart.

Result over [0, 60] (T = 60, C = 2): in use 59 min (s1/1 from 1); D = 1 on [10,60] (each repair hands its unit over in its own tick): down 50 min; 6 downtimes started (10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60); 5 complete repairs of 50 min (the one from 60 is not repaired by H); available = 120 - 50 = 70 min; idle = 70 - 59 = 11 min (2 on [0,1], 9 on [1,10]); utilization 59/120. Nothing completes: no lead time; s1/1's queue wait 0.

cases.title: a repair that hands its unit to a waiting failure wakes no held request and schedules no dispatch (D-074 (a) B, SIMULATION_SPEC §3; T-048 review round 2, L2)
derivation: The reviewer's N10 (T-048 review round 2, L2): capacity 2, TTF 10, TTR 5; s1/1 arrives at 1 and s2/1 at 12, each served 100 min, so neither completes by the horizon 40. Sequence numbers in parentheses.
t=0: arrivals s1 at 1 (1), s2 at 12 (2); FAILURE(0) at 10 (3), FAILURE(1) at 10 (4). t=1: s1/1 queues, DISPATCH (5) grants it (completion at 101, not scheduled).
t=10: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1: down (D=1), REPAIR(0) at 15 (6); FAILURE(1): idle = 2 - 1 - 1 = 0: waits.
t=12: s2/1 queues, DISPATCH (7): in use 1 + 1 > C - D = 1: held.

t=15: REPAIR(0): D=0, FAILURE(0) at 25 (8); the unit goes to the waiting failure 1: D=1, REPAIR(1) at 20 (9). The capacity did not rise, so the held s2/1 is not woken and no dispatch is scheduled (only a repair that no failure waits for wakes the held front).

t=20: REPAIR(1): D=0, FAILURE(1) at 30 (10); no failure waits: s2/1 wakes, DISPATCH (11): 1 + 1 <= 2: s2/1 [20, 120) (completion not scheduled). So s2/1's service starts at 20, in the event with sequence 11.
t=25: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 2 = 0: waits. t=30: FAILURE(1): idle 0: waits behind it; both wait to the horizon. 11 events.

A repair that also woke the held request after handing its unit over would add a DISPATCH at 15 (10) that holds s2/1 again: the same starts, downs, waiting failures and Result, but FAILURE(1) at 30 would take 11, s2/1 would start in the dispatch with sequence 12, and the run would process 12 events.

Result over [0, 40] (T = 40, C = 2): in use 39 (s1/1) + 20 (s2/1) = 59 min, utilization 59/80; down [10,15] and [15,20]: 10 min, 2 started, 2 complete repairs of 10 min; available = 80 - 10 = 70 min; idle = 70 - 59 = 11 min (2 on [0,1], 9 on [1,10]); nothing completes, 2 censored; queue waits 0 (s1/1) and 8 (s2/1, 12 to 20).
cases.simpy: not compared: failures 0 (from 25) and 1 (from 30) still wait at the horizon, which the script does not record

cases.title: an arrival and a repair in the same tick: the dispatch grants the arrival (D-048 golden 2)
derivation: m: FAILURE at 3 (idle: down until 5). s1/1 arrives at 5.
t=5: ARRIVAL (10) queues and asks for a dispatch; REPAIR (15): D=0, FAILURE at 8; s1/1 is a candidate, not held, so the repair wakes nothing; DISPATCH (20): s1/1 [5,6].
t=8: FAILURE: idle, down until 10. t=10: REPAIR (at the horizon, processed), FAILURE at 13 (> horizon).
Result over [0, 10]: 1 completed, lead time 1, wait 0; in use 1 min, utilization 0.1; down [3,5] and [8,10]: 4 min, 2 started, 2 complete; available 6 min; idle 5 min.

cases.title: a 0-tick repair scheduled during a dispatch runs after it and dispatches again in the same tick (D-048 golden 4)
derivation: G-B1 (src every 1, a 1 min, qb capacity 1, b 3 min) with breakdowns on a's resource ma: TTF 3, TTR 0. Without breakdowns G-B1's facts hold: a starts 1,2,3,5,8,11,14,17,20; b starts 2,5,8,11,14,17,20; blocks at a [4,5], [6,8], [9,11], [12,14], [15,17], [18,20].

t=3: e2 leaves a (0) for qb, e3 arrives (10); FAILURE (15): ma is idle, down with TTR 0: REPAIR at 3 (15, later sequence), which runs before the dispatch (20): ma is up again, e3 [3,4]. A 0-length downtime [3,3].
t=4: e3 is blocked at a (qb full), keeping ma; e4 held. t=5: b grants e2, unblocking e3 (ma released, nothing waiting) and e4 [5,6].
t=6: e4 is blocked at a holding ma; FAILURE (15): idle = 1 - 0 - 1 = 0: waits (pending).

t=8: e2 leaves b (0); e8 arrives (10); DISPATCH (20): b grants e3 [8,11]; qb has room: e4 is unblocked and releases ma, whose unit goes down for the waiting failure (D=1) with TTR 0: REPAIR at 8, priority 15, scheduled during the dispatch; e5, the front of ma, wakes and is held (C - D = 0); the dispatch ends.
t=8, after it: REPAIR (15): D=0, FAILURE at 11; it wakes e5 and schedules a second DISPATCH at 8 (20), which grants e5 [8,9]: the tick does not go back, and e5 starts at 8 as in G-B1.

The same at 11, 14, 17 and 20: the failure is due while ma is held by the blocked entity, waits, takes ma when b's grant unblocks it, and is repaired in the same tick, followed by a second dispatch. The 20 one is at the horizon (its next FAILURE at 23 is not scheduled).

So starts, completions, blocks and every G-B1 Result member are G-B1's; ma adds 6 downtimes of 0 ticks (3, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20), 6 started and 6 complete (D-074 (d)), down 0, available C*T = 20 min, idle 20 - 19 = 1 min; rb has no breakdowns: only its blocked group, as in G-B1.
cases.simpy: not compared: D-048 tie-break (a 0-tick repair inside a tick)

cases.title: a held request that only a repair can let in is not a deadlock (B1 tells capacity-bound from release-bound; T-047 review round 2, I1)
derivation: The finite buffer q makes the kernel run the D-050 B1 check; m breaks down at 1 (idle: down until 11).

t=2: the only entity arrives and queues; the dispatch holds it (1 > C - D = 0). After the dispatch: nothing in service or in a delay, one held candidate: B1 asks whether it is release-bound, in_use + units > C, with the full capacity C: 0 + 1 > 1 is false, so it is capacity-bound (only a repair can let it in) and this is no deadlock. (With >= it would be reported as one: the mutant this golden kills.)
B2 at the end of tick 2: held, none of its bundle in use: in that state since 2, TTRmax 10 (constant): due by 12.
t=11: REPAIR: D=0, FAILURE at 12; the repair wakes the held request (capacity rose without a release) and dispatches: work [11,12].
t=12: it completes (0); FAILURE (15): idle, down until 22 (REPAIR > horizon, not scheduled).

Result over [0, 15]: 1 completed, lead time 10, q's wait 9; in use 1 min, utilization 1/15; m (the model has a finite buffer, so it lists blocked_ticks too): blocked 0, down 10 + 3 = 13 min, 2 started, 1 complete of 10 min, available 2 min, idle 1 min;
blocking: src can reach the finite buffer q: 0 blocks; q full (its one place taken) [2,11]: 9 min.
cases.simpy: not compared: the point is the kernel's B1 check

cases.title: G-D2 with a resource that breaks down beside the cycle: B1 still finds the circular wait at 7 (R1 bypassed, test-only)
derivation: G-D2's model and timeline (R1 bypassed in the test only), plus resource x (TTF 2, TTR 1) that no process needs: x's FAILURE and REPAIR events (2, 3, 5, 6; next failure at 8) touch no queue and wake nothing.
x's events at 2 and 5 come after the same tick's arrivals, which have a dispatch pending, so no check runs after them; at 3 and 6 the check runs and finds entities in service.
t=7: the SERVICE_COMPLETE of r0/src/3 at s1 blocks it; nothing is in service or in a delay; B1 reports the same deadlock as G-D2: tick 420000, r0/src/5 blocked at src since 300000.

deadlock.reason: the replication deadlocked at tick 420000: r0/src/5 is blocked at node src since tick 300000

cases.simpy: not compared: SimPy does not detect deadlocks (G-D2)

cases.title: B2: a bundle that can never be filled (R3 bypassed, test-only: 2 units of a resource that breaks down; ADR-026 D-050's second counterexample)
derivation: r has capacity 2, TTF 10 and TTR 10 per unit; x needs both units (R3 refuses it; the test bypasses the validator), y one. sx/1 arrives at 6, sy/1 at 5. t=0: arrivals of sx (6) and sy (5) in ID order, then FAILURE(0) and FAILURE(1) at 10.
t=5: sy/1 [5,20]. t=6: sx/1 is the front of r's FIFO and is held (1 + 2 > 2).
t=10: FAILURE(0): idle = 2 - 0 - 1 = 1: down until 20; FAILURE(1): idle 0: waits.

t=20: sy/1 completes (0): its unit goes down for failure 1 (D=2), REPAIR(1) at 30; sx/1 wakes. REPAIR(0) (15): D=1, FAILURE(0) at 30. DISPATCH: 0 + 2 > 2 - 1: held. End of tick 20: sx/1 is held with no unit of its bundle in use: the B2 state since 20; TTRmax = 10: due by 30.

t=30: REPAIR(1) (scheduled at 20 before FAILURE(0)) runs first: D=0, FAILURE(1) at 40, sx/1 wakes; FAILURE(0): idle 2: down (D=1) until 40; DISPATCH: held again. The two clocks are now 10 apart: one unit is always down, for ever.
End of tick 30 (no other event at 30): sx/1 is still in the state and 30 >= 30: ErrStalled at 30 min (1800000), r0/sx/1 at x, since 1200000, due by 1800000.

stalled.reason: the replication stalled at tick 1800000: r0/sx/1 waits for node x since tick 1200000 with none of its bundle in use; it was due by tick 1800000

cases.simpy: not compared: SimPy does not detect stalls

cases.title: no stall at the deadline tick when the repair comes later in that tick (B2 at the end of a tick, D-074 (c))
derivation: G-F1 plus a one-off source sd at 13 that goes straight to done (no queue, no dispatch). sd sorts before src, so the first arrivals are scheduled sd, src, then m's FAILURE at 10; G-F1's timeline is unchanged.
e5 (r0/src/5) is held from 10 with nothing of its bundle in use: the B2 state since 10, TTRmax 3, due by 13.

t=13: ARRIVAL sd/1 (10) completes at once, without a dispatch. A B2 check right after it would see 13 >= 13 and report a stall; but REPAIR (15) is still due in tick 13: it wakes e5 and the dispatch grants it [13,14]. B2 checks only at the end of a tick, so nothing is reported.
Facts and Result: G-F1's, plus sd/1 completed at 13 with lead time 0 (15 completed, 16 created, 1 censored).
cases.simpy: not compared: the point is the kernel's B2 check
